answer:
We need
\[
n^2+n+1\equiv 0\pmod 7.
\]
The discriminant is
\[
1-4=-3\equiv 4\pmod 7,
\]
so
\[
n\equiv \frac{-1\pm2}{2}\equiv 2 \text{ or }4\pmod 7.
\]

Since
\[
1000=7\cdot142+6,
\]
each nonzero residue class \(1,2,\ldots,6\) occurs \(143\) times among \(1,\ldots,1000\). Thus both qualifying classes occur \(143\) times.

\[
\boxed{286}
\]
